verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew safely returned to Earth on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA’s Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down... on Friday, April 10'; R2: 'NASA’s Artemis II astronauts have returned safely to Earth... on Friday'; R3: 'SPLASHDOWN! NASA’s Artemis II crew... back on Earth... at 8:07 p.m. EDT'; R5: 'Artemis II crew splashes down... April 10, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm safe return via splashdown on the specified date, Friday, April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splash down off the coast of San Diego at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) on Friday, April 10'; R2: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California at 5:07pm local time'; R3: 'parachute-assisted splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'
verifications.reasoning: Exact location, time, and timezone match across sources.

verifications.claim: The four astronauts concluded a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately 10-day journey'; R2: '10-day journey'; R3: 'approximate 10-day mission around the Moon and back'; R6: '10-day journey'; R7: '10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: All sources consistently describe the mission duration as approximately 10 days, concluded by four astronauts.

verifications.claim: The mission marked the first human trip to the Moon and back in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'first crewed mission to travel around the Moon in more than 50 years'; R6: 'first people to travel to the Moon in more than half a century'; R7: 'first humans in over 50 years to venture to the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state it as the first crewed lunar trip in over 50 years since Apollo.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule touched down in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown... in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R2: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean'; R3: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'; R5: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources confirm Orion's splashdown (touchdown) in the Pacific Ocean.

verifications.claim: Recovery teams were stationed to retrieve the crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'recovery teams will retrieve the crew'; R2: 'Recovery teams were already in position'; R3: 'The recovery team is on site and headed to the capsule'; R5: 'U.S. Navy sailors on a dive medical, first contact team'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly mention recovery teams positioned and retrieving the crew post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: The astronauts were reported as "happy and healthy" following the high-speed re-entry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6 title: 'Artemis II crew 'happy and healthy' after completing historic mission'; R2: 'in good condition'; R7: '“What a journey. We are stable. Four green crewmembers”'; R3: 'safely extracted... feeling great, happy to be home'
verifications.reasoning: Exact phrase in R6 title and cited snippet; synonymous reports of good health post-reentry in others.

verifications.claim: The crew was transported to the USS John P. Murtha for initial medical evaluations.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'deliver them to the USS John P. Murtha. Once aboard, the astronauts will undergo post-mission medical evaluations'; R3: 'safely aboard the USS John P. Murtha, where they will undergo post-mission medical evaluations'; R7: 'on board the USS John P. Murtha recovery vessel'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm transport to USS John P. Murtha specifically for medical evaluations.

verifications.claim: The crew returned to NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'board an aircraft bound for NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston'; R3: 'board a NASA aircraft bound for the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston'; R4: 'returning to HOUSTON'; R5: 'return to Mission Control in Houston'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state crew transport to Johnson Space Center in Houston post-recovery.

verifications.claim: The mission successfully tested the systems needed to send future astronauts back to the Moon and eventually to Mars.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'confirm the systems necessary to support astronauts in deep space exploration and prepare to establish a sustained presence on the Moon'; R4: 'returning humans to the Moon and eventually sending astronauts to Mars'; R5: 'pave the way for humanity's return to the lunar surface'; R2: 'testing systems designed for future missions'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm successful testing of systems for future Moon missions; Mars is program goal explicitly linked.
